In industry, the use of membership fees with the collaboration holding IP rights is a standard model, allowing for both long-term success of the organization and shared governance for adding features and providing maintenance. Examples of such organizations are the PCI-SIG[2] and MPEG[3]. The licensing terms and membership cost for such organizations tend to be seen as too high for the operations teams in government and academic facilities that tend to run particle accelerators, although other divisions at the same facilities tend to be active members of such groups for computing, semiconductor technology, or video handling. 2.4 Partnership agreements and models It is necessary to highlight the extent to which the number of different partnership agreement models has proliferated for working with national lab subcontractors, and the lack of any clear path towards how a national lab accelerator facility can be involved in a third-party managed collaboration with multilateral MOU requirements. As an example of the complexity non-government partners need to navigate, in 2017 there were eight (8) different partnership agreement models available, of which none generally involved a lab joining an ex- isting collaboration on an equal or subservient footing with another non-national-lab entity (summarized below) [20]. While several of these mechanisms have characteristics beneficial for multilateral data shar- ing and collaboration between entities, shared software and collaboration does not cleanly fit within these guidelines unless a collaboration is itself a non-profit with the resources to manage such agreements. CRADAs The participants collaborate by providing personnel, services, facilities, or equipment and pool the results from a particular R&D program. SPPs SPPs permit DOE Laboratories to conduct work for other Federal agencies and nonfederal entities on a 100% cost reimbursable basis. Agreement for Commercializing Technology (ACT) ACT contracts allow research and technology transfer projects with more-flexible intellectual property arrangements and other terms and condi- tions used more traditionally in industry agreements, including fixed pricing, advance payments, and performance guarantees. Technology Licensing Agreements (TLAs) Because of the laws and policies governing the licensing of federally funded research and DOE policies regarding IP, TLAs may include provisions such as march-in-rights, government use rights, and indemnification provisions.
